api/Frontend.Runtime.Impl.GameImpl.Battl.title: Class RtsNetGameMode | Panzer War Document
api/Frontend.Runtime.Impl.GameImpl.Battl.summary: Class RtsNetGameMode Online RTS (BattleUnitOwnership.md §25, server docs/rts.md): every player picks a lineup within the budget per wave and deploys it whole; the server lays it out at one of their side's spawn points. Once all of a player's units are gone they wait out the cooldown and deploy again. Units are ordered from the map (the offline commander's RtsCommandController) or driven one at a time. The server owns the clock, the prices, the scores and the outcome. A unit's last order rides its sync state, so whoever simulates it next (the host for a player who left, the owner after a rejoin) carries it on. api/Frontend.Runtime.Impl.GameImpl.Battl.summary: Class WarZoneNetGameMode War zone network game mode: the capture zone map, except a sortie is bought rather than granted. Every price is the server's; this only shows the table it resolved. A room may let a player keep several vehicles (BattleUnitOwnership.md §16.3 A7): while alive they buy more at the usual price, each holding at its spawn point until driven. EventReference 结构，不是可拖放的 ScriptableObject。请在检视面板的事件选择器中挑选真实事件，例如 event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "list", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.EventManager/Events", "fields": "Path,Guid/Data1,Guid/Data2,Guid/Data3,Guid/Data4", "search": "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit", "count": 5 }, "expect": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)" }, "capture": { "Data1": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 1, "as": "int" }, "Data2": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 2, "as": "int" }, "Data3": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 3, "as": "int" }, "Data4": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 4, "as": "int" } } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.EventManager/EventFromPath", "args": [ "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "parameter:/engine01_cockpit/zoom" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "eventReference": { "Path": "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit", "Guid": { "Data1": "${Data1}", "Data2": "${Data2}", "Data3": "${Data3}", "Data4": "${Data4}" } } } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 3. 参数数组 展开 playParams 并添加一个元素，填写 key = zoom、value = 0.5。PlayParm 的两个字段分别为 string 和 float，组件在播放前逐个调用 setParameterByName。本配方会先查询当前事件缓存，确认示例事件存在并定义了 zoom；换用其他事件时，应填写该事件实际拥有的参数名。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "playParams": [ { "key": "zoom", "value": 0.5 } ] } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent)/playParams/0/key" }, "expect": { "contains": "zoom" } } ] 4. 生命周期与距离 勾选 isCustomSoundMaxDistance，显示 customSoundMaxDistance 后填入 75；关闭覆盖时该字段隐藏。默认覆盖关闭、距离为 50。这里限制的是启用时是否开始播放，不是持续更新的声音衰减范围。 OnEnable 调用 Play。若此时相机距离超过上限，方法直接返回，靠近后不会自动重播；事件为空、音效池未准备好或音效包加载失败时也不会开始播放。禁用或销毁会取消尚未完成的等待：isStopEventOnDisable = true 时归还已有实例到池；设为 false 时走 ReleaseEvent 路径，不能据此保证声音立即停止。本例保持 true。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "isStopEventOnDisable": true, "isCustomSoundMaxDistance": true, "customSoundMaxDistance": 75 } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent)/customSoundMaxDistance" }, "expect": { "contains": "75" } } ] 配方验证了 prefab、事件引用和参数读回；实际音频输出、音效包加载和游戏内距离行为仍需运行时验证。

由 VehicleInfo.GetLoadGUID() 返回，两者含义不同，不要互相代填。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 CreateAsset 对应新建资产；inspect_set 的对象引用赋值对应拖放到引用槽。以下把新建的配置赋给独立的 VehicleData；只读字段仅查询。 [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/vehicleTextData", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/AssetName" }, "expect": { "contains": "TutorialTank" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/editorAssetGuid" }, "expect": { "contains": "${editorGuid}" } } ] 2. 设置生命值与视野 在 基础 分组下展开 基础数据（字段 PSParameter）。 在 摄像机控制 分组中找到 血量（PSParameter.Health，图中标记 1）。代码默认值为 1200，本例教学值也填 1200。 在 视野 分组中找到 观察范围（PSParameter.viewRange，图中标记 2）。允许范围是 220–5000，代码默认值为 220，本例教学值填 600。 保存资产，再重新选中该资产，确认 PSParameter.Health 与 PSParameter.viewRange 已写入目标资产，而不是其他资产。 PSParameter.Health=1200 和 PSParameter.viewRange=600 只是教学取值，不是官方平衡建议。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 路径使用真实代码字段名，不受编辑器语言影响。资产字段写入会保存；随后重新选择并读回断言。 [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health", "value": "1200" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange", "value": "600" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/SaveAssets", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "null" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health" }, "expect": { "contains": "1200" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange" }, "expect": { "contains": "600" } } ] 3. 高级参数 点击对应的 移动、开火、炮塔 或 多炮塔 标签页，再按下表寻找字段；杂项 位于标签页下方。 字段 Inspector 分组与含义 显示条件与读取行为 sharedGunData 共享主炮数据（开火） 始终显示；非空时 GetTankFireParam() 返回其中的 tankFireParameter。 TFParameter 主炮参数（开火） 仅当没有 sharedGunData 时显示；此时 GetTankFireParam() 返回它。 sharedTurretData 共享炮塔数据（炮塔） 始终显示；非空时 GetTurretParam() 返回其中的 turretParameter。 MTParameter 炮塔参数（炮塔） 仅当没有 sharedTurretData 时显示；此时 GetTurretParam() 返回它。 PTCParameter 履带参数（移动） 仅在 GetGroundType() 返回 TrackController（IsTrackController() 为真）时显示。 MultiFireSystemData 旧版多炮塔系统（弃用） 旧版多炮塔列表，新载具不要新增。 simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters 新版多炮塔系统 当前多炮塔配置列表，元素类型为 SimpleVehicleFireSystemParameter。 vehicleSelfExplosionParams 自爆数据（杂项） 元素类型为 VehicleSelfExplosionTextParameter 的数组，按数组元素填写。 PTCParameter 的显示由 GetGroundType() 的判定顺序决定：isStationary → Stationary，MechParameter.isMech → MechController，LuaVehicleControllerParameter.isLua → Lua，ShipControllerParameter.isShip → Ship，其余情况才返回 TrackController。因此只把模型做成履带车，并不保证该字段出现。 sharedGunData 和 sharedTurretData 是共享引用：多个载具指向同一资产时，修改会影响所有引用者；没有共享引用时才分别使用 TFParameter 或 MTParameter。教学样例保留了 sharedGunData 引用，所以该样例中 TFParameter 不显示；这对只练习生命值与视野的步骤没有影响。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 MCP 可按路径查询高级参数和显示条件，等价于定位数据。截图窗口目前不能自动选择 Odin 标签页；若新增教程需要标签页截图，应由 Codex 补该能力后再重拍。这里不改高级参数。 [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/sharedGunData" }, "expect": { "contains": "SharedGunData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/noSharedGunData" }, "expect": { "contains": "False" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/noSharedTurretData" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTankFireParam", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TankFireParameter" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTurretParam", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TurretParameter" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetGroundType", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TrackController" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PTCParameter" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/MultiFireSystemData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/vehicleSelfExplosionParams" } } ] 4. 检查 确认 AssetName 和 editorAssetGuid 未变，PSParameter.Health 与 PSParameter.viewRange 已写入目标资产。 Inspector 截图只能证明字段位置与分组，不能证明运行时效果；要确认实际表现，需要在游戏内做一次检查。 如果后续需要调整高级参数，先确认上表的显示条件，再去对应分组里寻找字段。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 "Tutorial_VehicleTextData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/AssetName" }, "expect": { "contains": "TutorialTank" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/editorAssetGuid" }, "expect": { "contains": "${editorGuid}" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health" }, "expect": { "contains": "1200" } }, manual/en/component/fmod-play-component..summary: Configure an FMOD Playback Component 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run fmod-play-component --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Fmod.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } This page describes FmodPlayComponent: a MonoBehaviour that plays a configured FMOD event when its GameObject is enabled. 1. Component Add FmodPlayComponent to the GameObject that should emit sound. This example saves the component in a separate Tutorial_Fmod.prefab for reuse. Place that object at the required sound origin when using it in a scene. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent" } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 2. Event eventReference is a private [SerializeField] EventReference struct, not a draggable ScriptableObject. Choose a real event in the inspector event picker, for example event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "list", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.EventManager/Events", "fields": "Path,Guid/Data1,Guid/Data2,Guid/Data3,Guid/Data4", "search": "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit", "count": 5 }, "expect": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)" }, "capture": { "Data1": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 1, "as": "int" }, "Data2": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 2, "as": "int" }, "Data3": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 3, "as": "int" }, "Data4": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 4, "as": "int" } } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.EventManager/EventFromPath", "args": [ "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "parameter:/engine01_cockpit/zoom" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "eventReference": { "Path": "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit", "Guid": { "Data1": "${Data1}", "Data2": "${Data2}", "Data3": "${Data3}", "Data4": "${Data4}" } } } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 3. Parameters Expand playParams, add one entry and set key = zoom, value = 0.5. The PlayParm fields are a string and a float, passed to setParameterByName before playback. The recipe queries the current event cache to confirm that the example event exists and defines zoom. For another event, use its actual parameter names. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "playParams": [ { "key": "zoom", "value": 0.5 } ] } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent)/playParams/0/key" }, "expect": { "contains": "zoom" } } ] 4. Lifetime and distance Enable isCustomSoundMaxDistance, then set the revealed customSoundMaxDistance to 75. The field is hidden while the override is off. The defaults are false and 50. This is a check before starting playback, rather than a continuously updated attenuation range. OnEnable calls Play. If the camera is too far away at that point, playback does not start or automatically resume when it gets closer. An empty event, an unavailable pool or a failed bank load also prevents playback. Disabling or destroying the component cancels pending waits. With isStopEventOnDisable = true, an existing instance is returned to the pool; false takes the ReleaseEvent path and does not guarantee immediate silence. Keep it true for this example. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "isStopEventOnDisable": true, "isCustomSoundMaxDistance": true, "customSoundMaxDistance": 75 } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent)/customSoundMaxDistance" }, "expect": { "contains": "75" } } ] The recipe verifies the prefab, event reference and parameter readback. Audible output, bank loading and in-game distance behavior still require runtime verification.

The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_VehicleTextData.asset", "sharedGun": "${fixture}/Tutorial_SharedGunData.asset", "vehicleData": "${fixture}/Tutorial_VehicleData.asset" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar_VehicleTextData.asset", "${asset}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar-SharedGun.asset", "${sharedGun}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/AssetPathToGUID", "args": [ "${asset}" ] }, "capture": { "editorGuid": { "regex": "\\(String\\) ([a-f0-9]{32})" } } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/AssetName", "value": "TutorialTank" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/editorAssetGuid", "value": "${editorGuid}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/sharedGunData", "value": "@asset:${sharedGun}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/fireSpread/aimTime", "value": "2" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/fireSpread/dispersion", "value": "0.35" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] } VehicleTextData is the ScriptableObject that holds a vehicle's configuration. This page covers selecting the asset, locating fields, entering values and checking the result in the Unity Inspector. 1. Select the asset In the Project window, select the .asset whose main type is VehicleTextData. Its create menu is A Panzer War - 装甲纷争/G Ground Vehicle - 地面载具/Base - 载具配置/Vehicle Configuration - 载具配置参数. If you create a new asset, assign it to vehicleTextData on the target VehicleData. The pictures use a separate teaching sample named Tutorial_VehicleTextData; select the actual vehicle asset you are authoring in your project. Check that AssetName (shown as Default Asset Name. Do not modify it!) and editorAssetGuid (shown as Asset GUID) belong to the target vehicle. Both are read-only and cannot be edited here. editorAssetGuid is the Unity authoring-asset GUID, not the queue vehicleGuid. The queue vehicle ID comes from VehicleInfo.GetLoadGUID(). The two are different and must not be substituted for each other. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions CreateAsset is the asset-creation equivalent; assigning a live object with inspect_set is the reference-slot equivalent. The sample is assigned to a separate VehicleData. Read-only identifiers are queried only. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleTextData)", "${fixture}/Tutorial_NewVehicleTextData.asset" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleData)", "${vehicleData}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/vehicleTextData", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/AssetName" }, "expect": { "contains": "TutorialTank" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/editorAssetGuid" }, "expect": { "contains": "${editorGuid}" } } ] 2. Set HP and view range Expand PSParameter. It is under the Base BoxGroup and is labelled Player State Params. Inside PSParameter, find PSParameter.Health under the Camera Control group; it is labelled HP. The code default is 1200, and this example also uses the teaching value 1200. In the same PSParameter, find PSParameter.viewRange under the Sight group; it is labelled View Range. The allowed range is 220–5000, the code default is 220, and this example uses the teaching value 600. Save the asset, then reselect it and confirm HP and View Range were written to the target asset rather than another one. HP=1200 and viewRange=600 are teaching values only, not official balance guidance. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Paths use real code field names and remain stable across UI languages. Asset writes save the asset; reselect and read back the values to verify. [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health", "value": "1200" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange", "value": "600" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/SaveAssets", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "null" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health" }, "expect": { "contains": "1200" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange" }, "expect": { "contains": "600" } } ] 3. Advanced groups Select the relevant Mobility, Fire, Turret or Multi-Turret tab before locating a field below. The Misc group is below the tabs. Field Inspector group and label Visibility and read behavior sharedGunData Shared Gun Data (Fire) Always shown; when set, GetTankFireParam() returns its tankFireParameter. TFParameter Tank Fire Params (Fire) Shown only when sharedGunData is empty; GetTankFireParam() then returns it. sharedTurretData Shared Turret Data (Turret) Always shown; when set, GetTurretParam() returns its turretParameter. MTParameter Turret Params (Turret) Shown only when sharedTurretData is empty; GetTurretParam() then returns it. PTCParameter Track Params (Mobility) Shown only when GetGroundType() returns TrackController, i.e. IsTrackController() is true. MultiFireSystemData Old Multi-Turret (Deprecated) Legacy multi-turret list; do not add it to new vehicles. simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters New Multi-Turret Current multi-turret list; each element is a SimpleVehicleFireSystemParameter. vehicleSelfExplosionParams Self Explosion Params (Misc) An array of VehicleSelfExplosionTextParameter; fill it element by element. PTCParameter visibility follows the order inside GetGroundType(): isStationary → Stationary, MechParameter.isMech → MechController, LuaVehicleControllerParameter.isLua → Lua, ShipControllerParameter.isShip → Ship, and only the remaining case returns TrackController. A tracked model does not by itself guarantee the field. sharedGunData and sharedTurretData are shared references: when several vehicles point to the same asset, edits affect every referencing vehicle; use TFParameter or MTParameter only when no shared reference is assigned. The teaching sample keeps a sharedGunData reference, so TFParameter is hidden there; this does not affect the HP and View Range steps above. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions MCP paths locate advanced data and visibility conditions directly. The capture window cannot yet select Odin tabs automatically; Codex must add that capability before a tutorial needs such a capture. This group does not alter advanced settings. [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/sharedGunData" }, "expect": { "contains": "SharedGunData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/noSharedGunData" }, "expect": { "contains": "False" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/noSharedTurretData" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTankFireParam", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TankFireParameter" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTurretParam", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TurretParameter" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetGroundType", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TrackController" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PTCParameter" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/MultiFireSystemData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/vehicleSelfExplosionParams" } } ] 4. Check Confirm AssetName and editorAssetGuid are unchanged and HP and View Range were written to the target asset. An Inspector screenshot proves only field positions and labels, not runtime behavior; confirm actual behavior with a check in game. If you later adjust advanced parameters, check the visibility conditions in the table above first, then look for the field in its group. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions This recipe verifies the asset reference, identifiers and persisted fields. The sample has no complete driveable model, so gameplay is not verified. A successful capture is not a runtime pass. [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/vehicleTextData/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_VehicleTextData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/AssetName" }, "expect": { "contains": "TutorialTank" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/editorAssetGuid" }, "expect": { "contains": "${editorGuid}" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health" }, "expect": { "contains": "1200" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange" }, "expect": { "contains": "600" } } ]

The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "template": "${fixture}/battleConfig.yaml.default", "custom": "${fixture}/battleConfig.yaml" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } 1. Find the configuration folder On Windows, look for the saves folder next to the game executable. On Android and iOS, look under saves in the game's persistent data directory. Use the connected MCP instance to query the application data paths. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEngine.Application/dataPath" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEngine.Application/persistentDataPath" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] 2. Copy and edit the template Launch the game to generate battleConfig.yaml.default. Copy it to battleConfig.yaml in the same folder and keep the template's version field. This example changes the ramming damage multiplier from its default of 1 to 1.25. ramDamageCoff: 1.25 Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.BattleConfigAuthoring/WriteTemplate", "args": [ "${template}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "battleConfig.yaml.default" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.BattleConfigAuthoring/WriteCopy", "args": [ "${template}", "${custom}", "1.25" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "battleConfig.yaml" } } ] 3. The game reads the configuration at startup and uses the defaults if the file is invalid or the version differs. The sample uses the project's YAML reader to verify a temporary file. Check the collision effect in game. manual/en/gameplay/crash-and-launch-prob.summary: Troubleshoot startup and back up saves 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run crash-and-launch-problems Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "sample": "${fixture}/saves/profile/example.txt", "backup": "${fixture}/backup/saves", "restore": "${fixture}/recovered/profile/example.txt" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } 1. Collect the failure details Record the game version, platform, error message and steps to reproduce it. Save the runtime log from the failing session before trying a fix. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEngine.Application/consoleLogPath" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.SavePath/File", "args": [ "example.txt" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "saves/example.txt" } }, { "tool": "logs", "arguments": { "count": 20 } } ] 2. Quit and back up your saves Quit the game completely. Copy the entire saves folder or archive it outside the app directory. On Windows it is beside the game executable. On Android and iOS it is under the app's persistent data directory. Back up mods separately if you need downloaded content. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.Directory/CreateDirectory", "args": [ "${fixture}/saves/profile" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "DirectoryInfo" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.Directory/CreateDirectory", "args": [ "${fixture}/backup" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "DirectoryInfo" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/WriteAllText", "args": [ "${sample}", "Documentation save fixture" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.FileUtil/CopyFileOrDirectory", "args": [ "${fixture}/saves", "${backup}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/ReadAllText", "args": [ "${backup}/profile/example.txt" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "Documentation save fixture" } } ] 3. Verify the backup and restore if needed Open the backup in a separate location and check that its files are readable and subfolders are intact. If you need to reinstall, verify that backup first, then use the official package for your platform. Quit the game after reinstalling and restore the files into the active saves directory. Keep the original backup until the game starts and loads your saves. The replay verifies copying and recovering a scratch backup, including its file contents. manual/en/gameplay/definitive-edition-tr.summary: Definitive Edition sign-in and license troubleshooting 中文 | English Forgotten password Choose Forgot password on the sign-in screen or open the official password reset page. Use the email address tied to your account and follow the page's verification instructions. No license after signing in Check that you signed in with the account that purchased Definitive Edition or holds its activation. See the official shop for license and download information. Startup or update failure Record the time, client version and exact error, then consult the runtime log. If the game cannot start, preserve your data using the startup and save backup guide.

Delivered the health-bar version of the T67 for testing (Android). 2022.5.7 Delivered the modular version of the SU 100 Y for testing (Android). 2022.5.6 SU 100 Y: testing PBR materials. 2022.5.5 Delivered the health-bar version of the SU 100 Y for testing (Android). 2022.5.4 Fixed the wrong armor type on the Maus's tracks and fenders. Fixed one of the ST-II's guns having no sound effect. T-54: mobility improved and suspension behavior refined.

manual/en/gameplay/runtime-log.html.summary: Enable and read runtime logs 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run runtime-log Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "marker": "${fixture}/log.debug" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } 1. manual/en/mod/amphibious-vehicles.html.summary: Configure an amphibious vehicle 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run amphibious-vehicles --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "vehicle": "${fixture}/Tutorial_AmphibiousVehicle.asset", "engine": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ShipEngine.asset", "buoyancy": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ShipBuoyancy.asset", "model": "${fixture}/Tutorial_AmphibiousBody.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } Start from an existing ground vehicle. This example keeps its ground drive and adds a ship controller. 1. Enable amphibious control In the Mobility tab of VehicleTextData, expand Ship Params. Leave Is Total Controlled From Ship off and enable Is Ship Controller Enabled. Set Auto Enter Ship Controller Type to When Center Of Gravity Drown. This setting switches to ship control once the wheels lose contact and the center of gravity is submerged. Ground contact switches control back. Use isShip for a vehicle controlled entirely as a ship. For passive water interaction, leave both ship settings off and use the separate PassiveWaterInteractParameter settings. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar_VehicleTextData.asset", "${vehicle}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/isStationary", "value": "false" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/ShipControllerParameter/isShip", "value": "false" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/ShipControllerParameter/isShipControllerEnabled", "value": "true" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/ShipControllerParameter/autoSwitchShipControllerType", "value": "WhenCenterOfGravityDrown" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Set up the propeller path, engine and buoyancy Place a propeller node in the model prefab and add its path relative to the model root under Propeller Path. The example uses MainBody/Propeller. In the Project window, open Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > G Ground Vehicle - 地面载具 > Shared Data - 共享数据. Create a Ship Engine - 船舶引擎 and a Ship Buoyancy - 船舶浮力 asset. The example sets maxSpeedInKnots to 12 and buoyancyObjectLength to 6. Back in Ship Params, assign the assets to Engine Data and Buoyancy Data. Save and verify After saving, check that the ground drive still uses TrackController, the ship controller is enabled, both shared assets are assigned, and the propeller path exists in the model. The example verifies the settings and path in the editor. Test the waterline, propulsion and controller switching with the complete vehicle on a map that has water. The runtime skill is for offline vehicles. Verification covers editor assets and the teaching package, not an in-game salvo. 1. Create a skill slot Add a skills group under CrewData.upgradableSkillContents and set the entry's friendshipRequirement to 0. Choose CrewSkillBuff for crewSkillRef, then ArtillerySkillConfig for its crewSkill. This is nested configuration rather than a standalone ScriptableObject. The configuration's version must equal GetVersion(), currently 3, or the skill is treated as incompatible. The recipe queries and writes that version. See the commander tutorial for basic setup and unlock conditions. The teaching commander reuses Aino's valid portrait references without changing that source commander. Configure your own portraits for production content; valid portrait references are required for packaging. }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/crewName/defaultName", "value": "${title}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Configure cooldown Set initialCdType = Ready and coolDownTime = 20 seconds. Ready starts fully charged; NotReady starts from zero. CustomRatio reveals customInitialCdRatio, the initially completed fraction of cooldown. A successful release resets the progress. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/upgradableSkillContents/0/skills/0/crewSkillRef/displayValue/crewSkill/initialCdType", "value": "Ready" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/upgradableSkillContents/0/skills/0/crewSkillRef/displayValue/crewSkill/coolDownTime", "value": "20" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/upgradableSkillContents/0/skills/0/crewSkillRef/SetValue", "args": [ "@asset:${asset}/upgradableSkillContents/0/skills/0/crewSkillRef/displayValue" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/crewName/defaultName", "value": "${title}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 3. Configure a shell group Expand spawnInfos and add one entry: dispersion = 10, attackAngle = 45, count = (2,4), timeDelay = (0,2) and fromDistance = 800. The integer count excludes the upper bound, so this example produces two or three shells. Each independently samples a delay of approximately 0–2 seconds. Set artilleryBulletData and add the matching loadName and actual BulletData reference to the same SafeRef's safeRefAssetProvider.assets. This example copies the existing 105-HE ammunition and uses the copied asset's GUID as the lookup key. Runtime matches that key to a reference; it does not automatically convert a display name or file path into ammunition. The local player's camera ray must hit a target. The spawn point adds an X-axis offset rotated around the global Z axis to that target point. At 45 degrees this changes both horizontal position and height; it is not a horizontal offset along the camera direction. dispersion is passed to the projectile. manual/en/mod/blender-axis-fix.html.title: Correct model axes in Blender | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/blender-axis-fix.html.summary: Correct model axes in Blender 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run blender-axis-fix Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_AxisCheck.fbx" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } Use these steps when a model needs a different local rotation basis. Work on a copy. 1. Adjust the rotation and export Select the object in Blender Object Mode. Press R, X, -90, then confirm. Press Ctrl+A and choose Rotation. Press R, X, 90, then confirm. Export an FBX and import it into Unity. The Blender script regenerates the teaching example. The Unity MCP recipe below imports the resulting sample FBX. blender --background --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python Tools/ManualMcp/BlenderAxisFix/build_model.py -- Tutorial_AxisCheck.fbx Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Editor/DocumentationSamples/blender-axis-fix/Tutorial_AxisCheck.fbx", "${asset}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${asset}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Check the model's forward and up directions In Unity, verify that the front points along +Z and the top along +Y. Also check the turret's rotation axis and the gun's direction. The sample puts NoseMarker at (0, 0, 1) and RoofMarker at (0, 1, 0). Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/NoseMarker/transform/position" }, "expect": { "contains": "(0.00, 0.00, 1.00)" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/RoofMarker/transform/position" }, "expect": { "contains": "(0.00, 1.00, 0.00)" } } ] For other axis issues, check the source model's local axes, FBX export options and Unity import settings. See vehicle basics for hierarchy setup.

manual/en/mod/fixed-angle-reload.html.title: Fixed-Angle Reload Configuration | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/fixed-angle-reload.html.summary: Fixed-Angle Reload Configuration 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run fixed-angle-reload --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "sharedGun": "${fixture}/Tutorial_FixedAngleReload_SharedGunData.asset", "vehicle": "${fixture}/Tutorial_FixedAngleReload_VehicleTextData.asset" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar-SharedGun.asset", "${sharedGun}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar_VehicleTextData.asset", "${vehicle}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } } ] } Fixed-angle reload uses the gun buff TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff. After firing or switching shell type, it can wait for a configured delay, constrain turret angles and scale rotation speeds. The constraint is removed after reloading finishes. 1. Prepare shared gun parameters In the Project window choose Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > G Ground Vehicle - 地面载具 > Shared Data - 共享数据 > Gun - 炮管 to create SharedGunData. Expand tankFireParameter and find the Buffs reference list, buffRefs. This recipe copies an existing gun configuration to preserve its initialization data. Editing shared gun data affects all referencing vehicles. For a change to one vehicle, create a separate shared-data copy, or clear that vehicle's sharedGunData before editing its own TFParameter. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${sharedGun}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter" }, "expect": { "contains": "TankFireParameter" } } ] 2. Add the fixed-angle reload buff Add an entry to buffRefs, choose TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff and expand its configuration. Use these teaching values: Field Teaching value and meaning hasDelay / delay Enable the delay and set it to 0.5 seconds isTraverseLocked Enable Lock Traverse hasSpecificTraverseAngle / specificTraverseAngle Enable the specific traverse angle and set 0 degrees hasSpecificElevationAngle / specificElevationAngle Enable the specific elevation angle and set 5 degrees isOverrideTraverseSpeed / overrideTraverseSpeedCoff Override traverse speed with -0.5, a 50% reduction isOverrideElevationSpeed Leave disabled to preserve elevation speed Delay, angle and speed-coefficient fields are shown when their respective switches are enabled. When no specific angle is supplied, the code uses the current angle on entering the fixed-angle state. These values illustrate configuration only. The current list is AbstractTankFireBuffCasterSafeRef[]; the legacy buffs field is deprecated. The MCP recipe creates a real SafeRef entry by supplying both its type and configuration JSON. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Whole-array JSON assignment creates real SafeRef entries with the type name and serialized configuration. The recipe verifies persisted data and leaves deprecated buffs untouched. [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/buffRefs", "value": "[{\"fullName\":\"ShanghaiWindy.Core.TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff\",\"className\":\"ShanghaiWindy.Core.TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff, Core\",\"json\":\"{\\\"hasDelay\\\":true,\\\"delay\\\":0.5,\\\"isTraverseLocked\\\":true,\\\"hasSpecificTraverseAngle\\\":true,\\\"specificTraverseAngle\\\":0,\\\"hasSpecificElevationAngle\\\":true,\\\"specificElevationAngle\\\":5,\\\"isOverrideTraverseSpeed\\\":true,\\\"overrideTraverseSpeedCoff\\\":-0.5,\\\"isOverrideElevationSpeed\\\":false}\",\"safeRefAssetProvider\":{\"assets\":[]}}]" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/buffRefs/0/fullName" }, "expect": { "contains": "TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/buffRefs/0/json" }, "expect": { "contains": "\"specificElevationAngle\":5" } } ] 3. Bind it to a vehicle Assign the shared gun asset to VehicleTextData.sharedGunData. When set, GetTankFireParam() reads that asset's tankFireParameter. Without a shared reference, it reads the vehicle's TFParameter. Save and read the buff configuration back to confirm the intended asset is used. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/sharedGunData", "value": "@asset:${sharedGun}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/GetTankFireParam()/buffRefs/0/json" }, "expect": { "contains": "\"overrideTraverseSpeedCoff\":-0.5" } } ] 4. Check Verify the type, delay, angles, speed coefficient and shared reference. Runtime code removes the constraint through a periodic check after reloading completes. This tutorial does not verify the in-game constraint or restoration behavior. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions These calls verify editor configuration, shared references and persistence. Fixed angles, speed scaling and restoration after reload still require an in-game check. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/SaveAssets", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/buffRefs/0/json" }, "expect": { "contains": "\"delay\":0.5" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/sharedGunData/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_FixedAngleReload_SharedGunData" } } ]

manual/en/mod/hitbox-naming-conventions..summary: Damage model naming rules 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run hitbox-naming-conventions --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "external": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ExternalSource.prefab", "internal": "${fixture}/Tutorial_InternalSource.prefab", "armor": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ImportedArmor.prefab", "module": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ImportedModule.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } The damage model editor reads armor and internal module settings from mesh node names. The examples below apply to the vehicle's VehicleHitBox asset. 1. Prepare the source models Import the external armor and internal modules into Unity as separate models. Rename the mesh nodes, then assign each model to ExternalArmorModel or InternalModuleModel. The importer processes nodes with a MeshFilter. The teaching recipe creates two separate source models. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${external}", "mode": "create", "component": "UnityEngine.Transform", "children": [ "Plate_100", "Plate_100_Inter", "Plate_100_React" ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${external}", "mode": "update", "component": "UnityEngine.MeshFilter", "child": "Plate_100", "references": [ { "property": "m_Mesh", "asset": "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Light/AuthoringSamples/Square.obj", "type": "UnityEngine.Mesh" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${external}", "mode": "update", "component": "UnityEngine.MeshFilter", "child": "Plate_100_Inter", "references": [ { "property": "m_Mesh", "asset": "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Light/AuthoringSamples/Square.obj", "type": "UnityEngine.Mesh" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${external}", "mode": "update", "component": "UnityEngine.MeshFilter", "child": "Plate_100_React", "references": [ { "property": "m_Mesh", "asset": "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Light/AuthoringSamples/Square.obj", "type": "UnityEngine.Mesh" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${internal}", "mode": "create", "component": "UnityEngine.Transform", "children": [ "Transmission_120_15" ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${internal}", "mode": "update", "component": "UnityEngine.MeshFilter", "child": "Transmission_120_15", "references": [ { "property": "m_Mesh", "asset": "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Light/AuthoringSamples/Square.obj", "type": "UnityEngine.Mesh" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 2. Generate external armor The second segment is the integer armor thickness. Use Inter for spaced armor and React for reactive armor. Node name Armor type Thickness Plate_100 Normal 100 Plate_100_Inter Intermittent 100 Plate_100_React Reactive 100 In the damage model editor, click Generate External Armor. Move the generated armor under the corresponding parent nodes. See reactive armor for the extra settings on a reactive plate. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.VehicleHitBoxModelImport/ImportPrefab", "args": [ "${external}", "${armor}", "false" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] 3. Generate internal modules In Transmission_120_15, the segments identify the module type, hit points and module armor in that order. Type names are case-sensitive. The importer rounds the two numeric values up to integers. Include all three segments. Click Generate Internal Armor, then move the generated modules under their corresponding parents. The numbers in the screenshot match the segments of the node name. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.VehicleHitBoxModelImport/ImportPrefab", "args": [ "${internal}", "${module}", "true" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] 4. Save and verify Save the damage model prefab and check the HitBox and InternalModule fields. The recipe runs the same import processing in isolated prefabs. It verifies all three armor types and thickness values, plus the transmission's hit points and armor. manual/en/mod/install-git.html.summary: Installing Git 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run install-git Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. Assign fan, smoke or gearLights as needed. On aircraft, read the initial gear state and update the lights with FlightAPI.OnGearChanged. Pass self.script as the subscription owner and turn off per-frame updates for this branch. The ground branch uses TankAPI.GetEngineState, which returns success, RPM, RPM percentage, gear, speed and reverse status. Multiply RPM by 6 to get degrees per second. The example scales the fan speed by 0.1 and shows smoke above 80 percent RPM. Behavior() Property = { fan = { type = "object", value = nil }, smoke = { type = "object", value = nil }, gearLights = { type = "object", value = nil }, } local EngineAndGear = class("EngineAndGear") function EngineAndGear:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) self.vehicle = vehicle if VehicleAPI.IsFlightVehicle(vehicle) then if self.gearLights ~= nil then self.gearLights:SetActive(FlightAPI.IsGearDown(vehicle)) FlightAPI.OnGearChanged(self.script, vehicle, function(isDown) self.gearLights:SetActive(isDown) end) end self.vehicle = nil self.script:SetUpdateEnabled(false) return end self.script:SetUpdateEnabled(self.fan ~= nil or self.smoke ~= nil) end function EngineAndGear:OnUpdated(dt) if self.vehicle == nil then return end local ok, rpm, rpmPercent = TankAPI.GetEngineState(self.vehicle) if not ok then return end if self.fan ~= nil then self.fan.transform:Rotate(0, 0, rpm * 6 * dt * 0.1) end if self.smoke ~= nil then self.smoke:SetActive(rpmPercent > 80) end end return EngineAndGear Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Copy", Assign the object with the Animator to animator and set triggerName to the matching Trigger parameter in its controller. The example uses Destroyed. ModuleDestroyedTrigger:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) local module = InternalModuleAPI.GetInternalModule(self.gameObject) if module == nil or self.animator == nil then return end local animator = ComponentAPI.GetNativeComponent(self.animator, "Animator") if animator == nil then return end local wasDestroyed = InternalModuleAPI.IsDestroyed(module) InternalModuleAPI.OnStateChanged(self.script, module, function() local destroyed = InternalModuleAPI.IsDestroyed(module) if destroyed and not wasDestroyed then animator:SetTrigger(self.triggerName) end wasDestroyed = destroyed end) end return ModuleDestroyedTrigger Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Copy", "args": [ It is equivalent to item.add(item, 3). In function item:add(n), the first parameter is implicitly named self. Use a dot for ordinary functions that receive no instance. Compare the calls in Lua local item = { total = 2 } function item:add(n) return self.total + n end assert(item:add(3) == 5) assert(item.add(item, 3) == 5) assert(math.abs(-3) == 3) With item.add(3), Lua assigns 3 to self and leaves n without an argument. To pass a method to an event, see Keep self in a Lua callback. end

assert(item.add(item, 3) == 5)

manual/en/mod/lua-vehicle-init-timing.ht.title: Vehicle initialization timing | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/lua-vehicle-init-timing.ht.summary:
Vehicle initialization timing 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-vehicle-init-timing Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "script": "${fixture}/VehicleTiming.lua", "prefab": "${fixture}/Tutorial_VehicleTiming.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } On Lua API 2 or later, put code that needs assembled vehicle components in OnVehicleReady. The script runs OnStarted first. If the vehicle is already assembled, OnVehicleReady follows immediately. Otherwise it runs once after assembly. Bind the script to a LuaBehaviorMono on the vehicle. Put your component setup in InitVehicleDependencies. On older clients, resolve the vehicle with TryGetTankInitSystem, then check IsLoaded or subscribe to the loaded event. The example removes its legacy subscription when the behaviour is destroyed. Behavior() Property = {} local VehicleTiming = class("VehicleTiming") function VehicleTiming:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) if vehicle == nil or self.vehicle ~= nil then return end self.vehicle = vehicle self:InitVehicleDependencies() end function VehicleTiming:InitVehicleDependencies() print("[VehicleTiming] vehicle is ready") end function VehicleTiming:OnStarted() if (GAME_API_VERSION or 1) >= 2 then return end local found, vehicle = self.script:TryGetTankInitSystem() if not found or vehicle == nil then return end if vehicle.IsLoaded then self:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) return end self.legacyVehicle = vehicle self.legacyLoaded = function() self:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) end VehicleAPI.RegisterVehicleLoadedEvent(vehicle, self.legacyLoaded) end function VehicleTiming:OnDestroyed() if self.legacyLoaded ~= nil then VehicleAPI.UnRegisterVehicleLoaedEvent(self.legacyVehicle, self.legacyLoaded) self.legacyVehicle = nil self.legacyLoaded = nil end end return VehicleTiming Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Copy", "args": [ "../../Docs/Manual/tutorials/lua-vehicle-init-timing/example.lua", "${script}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${script}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${prefab}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorMono", "children": [], "references": [ { "property": "luaBehavior", "asset": "${script}", "type": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorScript" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${prefab}/LuaBehaviorMono/luaBehavior/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String) VehicleTiming" } } ] The replay checks that API 2 skips the legacy subscription, and that the legacy path waits and unregisters. Check actual assembly timing in game. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.AssetBundleManager/LuaEnv/DoString", "args": [ "local E = setmetatable({ Behavior = function() end, class = function() return {} end, print = function() end }, { __index = _G })
local subscriptions, removals, inits = 0, 0, 0
local callback
E.VehicleAPI = {
 RegisterVehicleLoadedEvent = function(v, cb) subscriptions = subscriptions + 1; callback = cb end,

}

local B = assert(loadfile('../../Docs/Manual/tutorials/lua-vehicle-init-timing/example.lua', 't', E))()
local function instance(t) return setmetatable(t, { __index = B }) end
local vehicle = { IsLoaded = false }
local script = { TryGetTankInitSystem = function() return true, vehicle end }
local init = function() inits = inits + 1 end
E.GAME_API_VERSION = 2
local current = instance({ script = script, InitVehicleDependencies = init })
current:OnStarted()
assert(subscriptions == 0 and current.vehicle == nil)
current:OnVehicleReady(vehicle)
current:OnVehicleReady(vehicle)
assert(inits == 1 and current.vehicle == vehicle)
E.GAME_API_VERSION = nil
local legacy = instance({ script = script, InitVehicleDependencies = init })
legacy:OnStarted()
assert(subscriptions == 1 and legacy.vehicle == nil)
callback()
callback()
assert(inits == 2 and legacy.vehicle == vehicle)
legacy:OnDestroyed()
assert(removals == 1)
return "Lua example passed"

manual/en/mod/material-component.html.title: Configure Vehicle Material Overrides | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/material-component.html.summary: Configure Vehicle Material Overrides 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run material-component --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "material": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Prop.mat", "settings": "${fixture}/Tutorial_MaterialSettings.asset", "model": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Material.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } This example configures transparency in the DE project with Unity 2022.3.62f2. CoreRPMatData stores material parameters. CoreRPMatComponent supplies those parameters when the vehicle's resources load. 1. Prepare the source material Find the target Mesh Renderer in the model prefab and identify its material slot. The recipe copies an existing propeller material to Tutorial_Prop.mat and assigns it to the first slot of Tutorial_Material.prefab. For your own model, use its mesh and textures. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/Altius-U/Art/Default-FastProp.mat", "${material}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "create", "component": "UnityEngine.MeshRenderer", "values": { "m_Materials": [ {} ] }, "references": [ { "property": "m_Materials.Array.data[0]", "asset": "${material}", "type": "UnityEngine.Material" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 2. Create the material configuration In the Project window, choose Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > C Config - 配置 > SRP Material Config - SRP 材质配置 to create CoreRPMatData. Expand coreRPMatParams and add an entry. Set coreRPShaderType to Transparency. Expand transparencyMatParam. Set the color's alpha to 0.35 and smoothness to 0.4. Assign the same Material asset used by the Mesh Renderer slot to linkedMaterial. For a camouflage setup, select VehicleCamouflage. The hasMask and maskTex fields in vehicleCamoflageMatParam supply the mask to the selected shader. Consult that shader for its channel meanings. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.Data.CoreRPMatData)", "${settings}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${settings}/coreRPMatParams", "value": "[{\"coreRPShaderType\": 1, \"transparencyMatParam\": {\"color\": {\"r\": 1, \"g\": 1, \"b\": 1, \"a\": 0.35}, \"smoothness\": 0.4}}]" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${settings}/coreRPMatParams/0/linkedMaterial", "value": "@asset:${material}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 3. Attach the component Add CoreRPMatComponent to the target object. Leave isComponentBased off and assign Tutorial_MaterialSettings to matData. Multiple renderers can reuse this configuration. The component mode instead uses each indexCoreRPMatParams entry's index to select a slot on the same object's Mesh Renderer. Counting starts at zero. Check those indices when reordering material slots. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.CoreRPMatComponent", "values": { "isComponentBased": false }, "references": [ { "property": "matData", "asset": "${settings}", "type": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Data.CoreRPMatData" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 4. Save and check the references Save the prefab and read back the Mesh Renderer material, linkedMaterial and component matData references. During resource loading, the code matches the source Material object and applies the parameters to an instance. Check the visual result after loading the vehicle. This example verifies the editor assets and their parameters. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/MeshRenderer/sharedMaterials/0/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_Prop" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${settings}/coreRPMatParams/0/linkedMaterial/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_Prop" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/CoreRPMatComponent/matData/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_MaterialSettings" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${settings}/coreRPMatParams/0/transparencyMatParam/color/a" }, "expect": { "contains": "0.35" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${settings}/coreRPMatParams/0/transparencyMatParam/smoothness" }, "expect": { "contains": "0.4" } } ]

manual/en/mod/mod-env-setup-hub.html.title: Set up a mod project with GameHub | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/mod-env-setup-hub.html.summary: Set up a mod project with GameHub 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run mod-env-setup-hub Create a project in GameHub, then open it in Unity Hub. You can also start from the Mod SDK ZIP. 1. Create the project with GameHub In GameHub, select Create Project and choose an empty folder. Copy the path when GameHub finishes creating the project. Read m_EditorVersion in the generated project's ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt and follow the Unity version guide. 2. Open the project with Unity Hub In Unity Hub, select Projects → Add → Add project from disk and choose the path you copied. Open the project and wait for import and compilation to finish. Complete the GameHub and Unity Hub steps manually. The MCP recipe checks the open project. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "editor_status", "arguments": {}, "expect": { "contains": "\"projectPath\"" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/ReadAllText", "args": [ "ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "m_EditorVersion:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Exists", "args": [ "Packages/manifest.json" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } } ] 3. Bind the Steam game content Set the Steam game folder if you need the game assets in the Editor. Start with vehicle basics, the map wizard, or the voice pack walkthrough.

manual/en/mod/modding-issue-archive.html.summary: Modding issue archive 中文 | English These issues and troubleshooting steps come from older versions of the tools. The screenshots show the settings and menu locations from those versions. 1. Map invisible collision Symptom: An invisible collision exists somewhere on the map, blocking objects or shell trajectories in that area. Check used at the time: Select all objects and look for a green collision box covering that area; check whether an extra Mesh Collider was duplicated, or whether the Mesh Collider was placed somewhere other than the visual model. 2. Slow suspension rebound, rolling over when turning Symptom: Suspension rebounds slowly and the vehicle tends to roll over while turning. Check used at the time: Check the Wheel Collider settings. The screenshot below was called the "default suspension configuration" in the old document and is a historical example only. 3. Map shell collision and render layers The original guide recorded its map shell collision and render layer settings in this screenshot. 4. Duplicate materials in Blender Symptom: Duplicate materials appear after duplicating objects in Blender. The original guide compared the materials produced by two duplication methods. Check the keymap and resulting materials in your own Blender version. Historical screenshot: duplicate materials after using ctrl c and ctrl v. Historical screenshot: result of duplicating an object with shift + d.

The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_RenderCheck.prefab", "material": "${fixture}/Tutorial_RenderCheck.mat" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } 1. Check the material shader Select the model's material in the Project window. In the Inspector, check that its Shader supports the active render pipeline. The example reads the shader from a vehicle material and checks support on this machine. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/Altius-U/Art/Default-FastProp.mat", "${material}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${material}/shader/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "WindyVerse/Vehicle/FullPBR" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${material}/shader/isSupported" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } } ] 2. Check the Renderer and material slots Select the child object that draws the mesh. Check the enable box on its Mesh Renderer or Skinned Mesh Renderer component. Expand Materials and verify the material references. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "create", "component": "UnityEngine.MeshRenderer", "child": "Hull", "children": [ "Hull" ], "values": { "m_Enabled": true }, "references": [ { "property": "m_Materials.Array.data[0]", "asset": "${material}", "type": "UnityEngine.Material" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/Hull/GetComponent(MeshRenderer)/enabled" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/Hull/GetComponent(MeshRenderer)/sharedMaterial/shader/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "WindyVerse/Vehicle/FullPBR" } } ] 3. "OK:" }, "phase": "build" } ] } Build a separate .modpack for each target. The game requires AssetBundles built for the platform it runs on. Prerequisites Install the matching Unity version and platform modules. The project is registered in GameHub. If it is not, click Add Path in GameHub and point it at that Unity project. Local file: dependencies (adjacent UnityProject / Packages layout) resolve correctly, and the SDK dependency matches the build for this platform. Create the soft-linked project In GameHub, select the target platform you want to build for. GameHub creates a soft-linked project for that platform; click Copy to copy its path. Open Unity Hub, click Add project from disk, and enter the path copied in step 2. Click the version, change Current Platform to the platform of the project you created, make sure the name matches, then click Open. After the project opens, check the target in File → Build Settings and wait for import to finish. GameHub's linked projects share source assets. Each platform keeps its own Library. Follow the GameHub and Unity Hub steps manually, then use MCP to check the target of the open project. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions The sample checks the currently selected Windows target. Choose the required build platform in the Editor. [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.EditorUserBuildSettings/activeBuildTarget" }, "expect": { "contains": "(BuildTarget) StandaloneWindows64" } } ] Build and validate each platform separately For that platform, run Build Linked Objects to AssetBundle on the BuildPipeline. Then run Package Mod Now on the associated ModPackage. Keep the generated .modpack and its .modpack.json sidecar. Check the platform, Unity version, resource manifest and metadata, then test it in the game on that platform. After changing resources or switching platforms, repeat the first two build steps. The replay below verifies a Windows teaching package. Check Android and iOS builds on their corresponding platforms. manual/en/mod/physics-wheels.html.summary: Configure a Wheeled Vehicle 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run physics-wheels --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "vehicle": "${fixture}/Tutorial_WheeledVehicle.asset", "model": "${fixture}/Tutorial_WheeledBody.prefab", "collider": "${fixture}/Tutorial_WheelCollider.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } Current vehicles use the wheeled mode of TrackController. The legacy NPhysicCarController selection branch is disabled. When migrating an older model, check its wheel nodes and its current vehicle configuration first. 1. Prepare the hull and wheel nodes Start from the vehicle setup guide and place VehicleDynamics and Wheels under the same parent. The teaching prefab has a Rigidbody and four children under Wheels: FrontLeft, FrontRight, RearLeft and RearRight. On your model, place them at the corresponding axle positions. The picture shows the finished Mobility configuration. TankWheelCollider supplies the tire collider parameters and isWheelVehicle enables wheeled mode. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "create", "component": "UnityEngine.Rigidbody", "children": [ "VehicleDynamics", "Wheels/FrontLeft", "Wheels/FrontRight", "Wheels/RearLeft", "Wheels/RearRight" ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar_VehicleTextData.asset", "${vehicle}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/isStationary", "value": "false" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Group wheels by drive and steering Open the Mobility tab of VehicleTextData and expand PTCParameter. Assign a template prefab with a Unity WheelCollider to TankWheelCollider. The runtime wheels copy its radius, suspension and friction settings. A group can override this with steerData.wheelCollider. An empty group template falls back to the main template. Add two entries to steerableWheels. All wheels paths are resolved relative to the parent of VehicleDynamics. Group Paths isMotor isSteerable maxSteerAngle Front Wheels/FrontLeft, Wheels/FrontRight true true 28° Rear Wheels/RearLeft, Wheels/RearRight true false 0° Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar_WheelCollider.prefab", "${collider}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/PTCParameter/TankWheelCollider", "value": "@asset:${collider}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/PTCParameter/steerableWheels", "value": "[{\"wheels\": [\"Wheels/FrontLeft\", \"Wheels/FrontRight\"], \"steerData\": {\"isMotor\": true, \"isSteerable\": true, \"maxSteerAngle\": 28}}, {\"wheels\": [\"Wheels/RearLeft\", \"Wheels/RearRight\"], \"steerData\": {\"isMotor\": true, \"isSteerable\": false, \"maxSteerAngle\": 0}}]" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 3. Enable wheeled mode Enable isWheelVehicle in the same Mobility tab. This example uses no track data, so TrackData stays empty. Keep Stationary Base off so the ordinary ground vehicle uses TrackController. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/PTCParameter/isWheelVehicle", "value": "true" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/PTCParameter/TrackData", "value": "null" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 4. Save and check Save the hull and configuration, then check the mode, collider template, wheel paths and front steering angle. The recipe verifies the editor assets with teaching nodes. Test suspension, grip and steering after assembling a complete vehicle. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/GetGroundType()" }, "expect": { "contains": "TrackController" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/GetEngineParam()/isWheelVehicle" }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/GetEngineParam()/TankWheelCollider/WheelCollider/radius" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Single)" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/GetEngineParam()/steerableWheels/0/steerData/maxSteerAngle" }, "expect": { "contains": "28" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Wheels/FrontLeft/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "FrontLeft" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Wheels/FrontRight/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "FrontRight" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Wheels/RearLeft/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "RearLeft" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Wheels/RearRight/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "RearRight" } } ]
